phase3_findings.description: Only the JsonBoundsError arm of _bounded_request_metadata returns discarded=True; the meta-read-error, non-dict meta, key-iteration-error and unexpected-exception arms also drop the whole _meta but return ({}, False), so the refusal line reads kept _meta keys=[] as if the caller sent nothing.

RuleSetRequestError.refusal_class strips the 'Request refused: ' prefix by convention; a message lacking it becomes the whole class, and the passed-checks rule for identity fields lives only at raise sites. _refusal_kind in safety/rule_sets.py repeats the prefix parsing.

audit_line outcome is a free-form str and identity travels as dict[str, Any] splatted into audit_line(**identity); a misspelled key would raise TypeError inside the finally block and replace the call's result or exception.

metadata_discarded is a separate bool next to metadata, so a non-empty metadata with metadata_discarded=True is representable and refusal_log_fields would name no keys; the only producer keeps them consistent today.
RefusalRedactingRunner's branch for an UnsafeSqlError or RlsError no guard logged first now logs class and kept-key fields, but no test asserts them.
test_no_rule_set_file_writes_no_audit_or_refusal_line only checks no message contains 'rule-set', so a differently worded new refusal line on the no-rule-set path would pass.
